What does Marcus teach about living in the present moment?
</message>

<passage>
What remains to you of this life is little. Live as on a mountain. For it makes no difference whether we live here or there, provided we live like citizens everywhere in the world. Let men see and know you as a man indeed, living according to Nature. If they cannot endure you, let them slay you. It is better so than to live as they live.
</passage>

output.reason: Passage discusses living virtuously and according to Nature, not specifically the present moment.
